fitnessSpec.hiking: Strenuous - same Boston Basin approach as the West Ridge (~7 mi, 3,100+ ft gain) plus a longer technical day (8 pitches, ~10.5 hr).

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~5-6 hrs to Boston Basin camp, plus additional approach time to gain the east ridge proper.
requiredSkills: multi-pitch trad leading at 5.6 on loose rock
route-finding through towers and gendarmes
rappelling
stamina for a long, sustained technical day
sound retreat judgment on an exposed crest in changing weather
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced alpine trad leader comfortable with longer, more sustained routes and loose-rock route-finding among gendarmes.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Roundtrip on the order of 6-9 miles with ~2,800-3,200 ft of gain, including a pass crossing (Ingalls Pass) and off-trail talus/slab travel to the base of the ridge
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light alpine rack (small rack + a few slings, approach shoes swapped for rock shoes), roughly 15-20 lbs

partner_requirements.approachTime: Roughly 3-4 hours from the Esmeralda Basin trailhead via Ingalls Pass and the Ingalls Lake basin to the start of the ridge
requiredSkills: Leading/following 5.4 traditional or alpine rock
Multi-pitch rope management and efficient transitions
Routefinding on talus, slab, and an unmarked alpine ridge to gain and follow the route
Comfort on loose blocky rock and exposed, airy ridge terrain
Basic self-rescue / rappel competence for the descent
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate alpine rock climber - comfortable leading low 5th class (5.4) alpine rock with loose rock and moderate exposure, and competent scrambling on class 2-3 talus/slabs for the approach

fitnessSpec.hiking: Short, steep forest and talus approach from the SR-20 hairpin to the East Face
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Trad rack for sustained crack/face climbing, roughly 18-22 lb

partner_requirements.approachTime: Roughly 1 hour from the SR-20 hairpin pullout to the East Face
requiredSkills: 5.11+ crack and face leading
multi-pitch endurance across 12 pitches in a day
route-finding among adjacent East Face lines
efficient descent management
comfort with serious commitment typical of a grade V route
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Strong 5.11+ trad/free climber comfortable with sustained face and crack pitches and the commitment of a grade V, 12-pitch outing

fitnessSpec.hiking: Excellent — a remote glacier approach followed by sustained hard climbing
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Alpine rack plus glacier-travel gear, ~25-30 lb

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long, remote approach up the Ice Cliff Glacier to the base of the pillar; likely requires a bivy
requiredSkills: sustained hard crack climbing (5.10+)
glacier travel
self-sufficient multi-day alpine climbing
committing-retreat/rappel management
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Expert alpine rock climber and 5.10+ crack specialist with glacier-approach experience

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very strong — a ~13hr car-to-car day with large elevation gain/loss

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long — over Longs Pass and Ingalls Creek similar to the Cascadian approach, then gaining and following the west ridge over the False Summit
requiredSkills: easy trad multi-pitch leading (5.4)
extended 3rd/4th-class scrambling and route-finding among towers and notches
long alpine-day endurance
comfort with sustained exposure on an unmaintained ridge crest
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Competent 5.4 trad climber with extensive alpine scrambling stamina and exposure tolerance

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very high - multi-day trailless approach to Crescent Creek basin with sustained off-trail travel and elevation gain
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Heavy multi-day alpine kit typically 35-45+ lb for the approach

partner_requirements.approachTime: Multi-day approach to Crescent Creek basin given extreme remoteness of the range; not a single-push objective
requiredSkills: off-trail/bushwhack route-finding in trailless terrain
5.6 rock climbing on ledges and short rock steps, often in mountain boots with a pack
route-finding among towers to avoid wrong-summit errors
basic multi-pitch rope work
self-sufficiency for remote extraction
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced alpine climbers with North Cascades approach experience; the moderate rock grade (5.6) makes this the more accessible of Mount Terror's two routes, but the remoteness and route-finding demands still rule out newer alpine climbers

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong; sustained approach with an overnight pack into Boston Basin followed by a glacier approach to the base of the ridge the next day
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight/multi-day pack (camp gear, rack, glacier gear), roughly 35-45 lb

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~4-6 hrs to a Boston Basin camp, then ~1-2 hrs of glacier/snow approach to the base of the south ridge on climbing day
requiredSkills: glacier travel and crevasse rescue (approach crosses a glaciated basin)
5.6 traditional multi-pitch leading on alpine rock
route-finding among towers on the ridge crest
basic snow travel with axe and crampons
comfort downclimbing/rappelling on loose, blocky terrain
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid intermediate alpine climber with prior glacier-travel and multi-pitch alpine-rock experience; comfortable with loose rock and route-finding without a well-beaten path

fitnessSpec.hiking: Moderate off-trail approach fitness for the Kangaroo Ridge basin approach off SR 20, including talus/scree and brush
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light alpine rack (single rope, small trad rack, rap gear) - no glacier or heavy overnight gear needed for this short route

partner_requirements.approachTime: Roughly 1.5-2.5 hours from the SR 20 pullout near the Hairpin turn up into the Kangaroo Ridge basin, consistent with other short Kangaroo Ridge approaches
requiredSkills: 5.4 trad/multi-pitch rock leading
rappelling and anchor evaluation
loose-rock/choss management and careful movement
basic alpine route-finding on an infrequently-climbed line
thunderstorm awareness/bail judgment given exposed summit moves
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Comfortable multi-pitch trad rock climber with prior alpine rock experience; should be unfazed by loose rock and unfamiliar/older rappel anchors, and capable of independent route-finding since this isn't a heavily-trafficked line

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very high - a brutal, mostly off-trail approach via the Nooksack Cirque with brush, river fords, talus, and glacier travel to a high camp around 5,900 ft, followed by a very long (often 18-21 hour) summit push and descent
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Moderate-heavy overnight alpine load (glacier travel gear, technical rock rack, camp/bivy gear) carried through bushwhacking and boulder-hopping terrain, not maintained trail

partner_requirements.approachTime: Multi-day: typically a full day (6-10+ hrs) up the Nooksack Cirque via brush, river fords, and glacier travel to high camp, followed by a very long summit day (often 18-21 hrs round trip from high camp) that includes roughly ten rappels back down to the glacier
requiredSkills: Glacier travel and crevasse rescue (East Nooksack/Price Glacier approach)
Multi-pitch traditional leading up to 5.6 on loose, featured alpine rock
Route-finding on complex, unmarked, loose terrain
Steep snow/ice couloir climbing (reported up to ~50 degrees)
Building and trusting rappel anchors, including deadman/picket anchors, for a long multi-rappel descent
Strong off-trail navigation and bushwhacking stamina
Self-sufficiency and sound judgment - this is a remote committing objective with no realistic quick rescue
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced alpine climbing team only - a serious Grade IV North Cascades objective; partners should have prior success on remote, multi-day alpine rock routes with glacier approaches before attempting this

partner_requirements.fitnessSpec: Fit for a long, full-value day (~14.5-hr summit-and-exit day)
requiredSkills: Real snow/ice competence — self-arrest, crampon/axe on firm 30-40°+ approach couloir terrain that can hold firm snow/ice into July
Route-finding judgment — a ledge/gendarme maze near the top is repeatedly cited as the navigation crux
Brush/bushwhack tolerance on the Mountaineer Creek approach
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid 5.7-5.8 trad leader (crux can reportedly feel stiffer than 5.6)

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong - steep, sustained climber's trail and talus/scramble approach to Burgundy Col with significant elevation gain before any roped climbing begins
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Moderate-heavy alpine rack (25-35 lb) for the approach, cached or carried on the climb

partner_requirements.approachTime: Multi-hour steep approach to Burgundy Col and the Wine Spires bench camp (6,500 ft) before the technical climbing starts; typically a full day if climbing car-to-car, or an overnight camp for parties combining multiple spires
requiredSkills: trad leading on loose/suspect rock
multi-pitch anchor building and belay transitions
rappelling on loose rock (rope management, rockfall avoidance)
route-finding on an unmarked alpine approach and descent
comfort retreating/bailing from a committing position if weather turns
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid alpine rock leader comfortable at 5.8-5.9 on loose, run-out terrain; prior Grade III multi-pitch alpine rock experience (e.g. Liberty Bell group or similar North Cascades objectives) strongly recommended before attempting the Wine Spires

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strenuous — long Enchantments approach via Snow Lakes or Colchuck/Aasgard Pass
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Moderate-heavy on approach (rack, rope, overnight gear if camping); light for the climb day

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long — via Snow Lakes or Colchuck/Aasgard Pass to a Core Enchantments camp before gaining the south face
requiredSkills: Leading sustained 5.9 crack systems on alpine granite
Multi-pitch efficiency and route-finding on a long alpine face
Rope management and anchor-building on exposed rappels
Weather judgment for the long committing approach and climb
Wilderness permit planning for the Enchantment Permit Area
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate-advanced alpine rock climber comfortable leading sustained 5.9 crack pitches with real exposure

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong - long approach with roughly 7,000+ ft of cumulative gain (Longs Pass, drop to Ingalls Creek, climb to basin camp) typically split over 2 days, or pushed as a 14+ hour car-to-car day
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Moderate-heavy: rope, rack, and overnight/bivy kit carried over talus and boulder fields

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long, multi-stage approach (Longs Pass -> Ingalls Creek -> upper basin camp at ~7,400 ft); usually done as a 2-day trip
requiredSkills: exposed 4th-class scrambling
short 5.4 rock leading with gear placement
rappel and anchor building for the descent
judgment on loose/blocky rock
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate alpine climber - comfortable moving quickly on exposed 4th class and leading short pitches of low 5th class rock in a remote setting

fitnessSpec.hiking: strong all-day fitness - long approach/scramble day on an unmaintained climbers' path
fitnessSpec.packWeight: light day-pack, roughly 15-25 lbs (water, layers, light rack if linking with roped sections)

partner_requirements.approachTime: long - several hours to the ridge under normal conditions, plus an unbridged ford of the Middle Fork Nooksack near the trailhead
requiredSkills: Leading or simul-climbing easy fifth-class rock with real exposure
confident downclimbing / exposure tolerance
route-finding on sparsely marked climbers' paths
navigation via map/GPS through brush and talus off-trail
judging whether a river ford is safe at the current flow
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: solid alpine rock experience: comfortable on exposed 5.4 ridge terrain, building a rappel anchor, and downclimbing loose third-class gullies on the descent

requiredSkills: Comfortable on runout, blocky, loose terrain
Competent unroped 3rd/4th-class scrambling for the approach gully
Creek ford (Ingalls Creek) plus off-trail approach navigation
No snow/ice skills needed in-season
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Trad leader solid at 5.7-5.8 (variable rock quality near the base)

requiredSkills: Tolerance for 1,000s of feet of loose scree approach to ~8,700 ft — the real crux of the route
